title: Fix rollout step getting stuck when metric evaluation times out
author: Hannah Rivera
description: Context: During Hosted canary rollouts beta, we hit a failure mode where the rollout orchestrator could stall in a step transition if cohort metric evaluation timed out (telemetry query timeout / downstream lag). The UI would show the rollout as "Progressing" (or "Evaluating stop conditions") indefinitely, and subsequent actions (pause/rollback) were inconsistent depending on which region worker had the lock. This PR makes metric evaluation timeouts explicit and recoverable: we retry metric evaluation with bounded backoff, and if retries are exhausted we move the step into a terminal error state that is visible in Console and actionable (pause/rollback). Root cause: the orchestrator treated METRICS_EVAL_TIMEOUT as a transient internal error but did not update step state; the worker would release the lease without emitting a state transition, and subsequent runs would re-enter evaluation but keep hitting the same timeout due to identical query window, resulting in no forward progress and no clear operator signal. Fix: (1) Introduce an explicit evaluator result enum: OK | STOP_CONDITION_MET | INSUFFICIENT_DATA | TIMEOUT_RETRYABLE | TIMEOUT_EXHAUSTED | QUERY_ERROR. (2) Add retries for TIMEOUT_RETRYABLE with jittered backoff (default 3 attempts over ~90s) and a per-rollout "metrics_eval_deadline" so we don't retry forever across worker restarts. (3) On TIMEOUT_EXHAUSTED, transition the rollout step to ERROR with reason=METRICS_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT and include the last evaluator details (query window, service, attempt count). (4) Make the orchestrator action handlers (pause/rollback) tolerant of ERROR steps so customers can immediately rollback without needing an internal override. (5) Emit a telemetry/audit event when we enter this error state so SRE sees it and the customer sees it in the rollout timeline. UI/Console impact: Console now gets a stable error code to display: ROLLOUT_METRICS_TIMEOUT. In the activity panel, we record "Metric evaluation timed out" with retry attempts and a hint to adjust stop condition windows / check telemetry health. The workflow shows a primary CTA to rollback, and a secondary CTA to retry evaluation (manual "re-check"), which triggers a new evaluation window (now + lookback) rather than reusing the stuck window. Safety: No change to stop-condition semantics when metrics are available; only changes behavior when we cannot evaluate within the configured budget. We intentionally choose fail-closed for step progression: we do not automatically advance traffic if we cannot verify SLOs, but we also avoid indefinite stalls. Testing: Adds unit tests for evaluator retry behavior and state transitions; adds an integration test that simulates a telemetry query timeout and verifies we end in ERROR with an actionable message; updates one E2E test stub to accept the new error code. Rollout: This is a hotfix safe for beta tenants; gated behind existing rollouts orchestrator feature flag. After merge, we should deploy to staging, then enable for beta tenants in US-East first and monitor "rollout_step_error_total{reason=METRICS_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT}" and orchestrator loop latency. References: SUP-48302 (beta customer auto-paused after latency spike; investigation showed metric fetch timeouts under load) and incident thread 1740726110 (split mismatch follow-up highlighted need for clearer "stuck" states).
commits: rollouts/orchestrator: plumb explicit metric evaluator result codes and details
telemetry/evaluator: add bounded retry w/ jitter for timeouts; add deadline
rollouts/state-machine: persist step ERROR state for metrics timeout; allow pause/rollback transitions from ERROR
console-contracts: surface ROLLOUT_METRICS_TIMEOUT error code + details
tests: add evaluator retry unit tests + orchestrator integration test for timeout -> ERROR
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we ensure this doesn't retry forever across worker restarts? We've seen lease churn during deploys and don't want permanent "try again" loops.

Hannah Rivera (author): Yep — added metrics_eval_deadline persisted on the step (derived from first eval attempt + maxRetryDuration). On restart, we respect the deadline and move to TIMEOUT_EXHAUSTED once exceeded.
Aisha Bello: What alerts are we expecting off the new ERROR reason? We should page only if it's widespread; per-rollout errors should be visible but not pagey.

Hannah Rivera: Agreed. Emitting counter rollout_step_error_total{reason=METRICS_EVALUATION_TIMEOUT} + a rate-limited event. Paging is not part of this PR, but SRE can add a dashboard panel and an alert on sustained rate > threshold.
Jada Williams: State machine question: are pause/rollback allowed from ERROR? We need to ensure customers can always rollback without support.
Hannah Rivera: Yes. Updated transition guards to allow PauseRequested and RollbackRequested from ERROR steps. Also added a regression test for "rollback from ERROR".
Logan Wright: Any concern about changing telemetry query windows when user hits "re-check"? We should be explicit about which time range is used.
Hannah Rivera: Re-check starts a new evaluation window anchored at now with the configured lookback. We include the query window in evaluator details so UI can show it in the timeline.
Sean Gallagher: Requested change: please include attempt count + last error in the activity event for easier debugging.
Hannah Rivera: Done in 5th commit; activity payload includes attempts, last_error, and evaluator_deadline_ms. (Audit event remains minimal; activity timeline holds the verbose details.)
Sean Gallagher: LGTM after that, thanks.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Deployed to staging (canary) same day; production rollout to beta tenants scheduled via release checklist.
release_notes: Fixes a beta issue where Hosted canary rollouts could stall if cohort metrics evaluation timed out.
Adds bounded retries for metric evaluation timeouts and transitions to an explicit ERROR state when exhausted.
Improves Console-facing error messaging and rollout activity timeline for metrics evaluation failures.
Allows immediate pause/rollback actions even when a step enters ERROR due to metrics timeout.
